title: Whose voices survive on unidentified early wax cylinders?
short: Early recordings preserve speakers whose names are missing or disputed. Can the words on the cylinders and contemporary records identify them?
matters: Putting a name to a voice can recover who used the phonograph, who was meant to hear it, and how private speech and public performance first entered recorded sound.
stuck: Surface noise obscures names and announcements. Labels can be incomplete, and a cylinder may carry traces of an earlier recording. The probable identification of Frederick Dent Grant on EDIS 93953 provides a case to test.
solved: A proposed identification should fit several independent clues or match a named recording of the same performance, with enough evidence for another listener to check it.
approach: Start with short passages that name a place, person or sketch. Compare untouched transfers and documented restorations against family papers, programmes, trade catalogues and named recordings.
